content:
As the number of Mac AI agents requesting “full disk access” permissions surges, Apple says it will adjust macOS to protect user privacy.

Although Apple has not disclosed specific details, the company said users should understand the true implications of granting such “extremely high” permissions to applications.

Apple explained in a blog post on its Developer website that macOS’s full disk access feature was originally designed to “let backup applications function properly on Mac.” However, Apple noted that “some developers” use macOS full disk access in ways that may put users at risk.

In response, Apple said it will “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant such extremely high permissions to applications must do so through a very explicit user action.”

The company did not elaborate further on these controls or the planned changes. However, Apple said the rise of “increasingly capable and autonomous” AI agents is drawing attention to privacy and security concerns:

Apple made the announcement as tools such as Meta Muse and OpenAI’s Dots are gaining popularity. These always-on AI agents require access to large amounts of users’ personal data, and we have already seen some negative incidents involving Meta Muse.
